ambiguities: The narrator is present throughout as the visiting, listening consciousness at the barracks, but the passage never stages him as socially included, excluded, favored, or dismissed; he functions purely as observer/reporter of Saint-Loup's popularity, so no status effect is scored for him.

The aside that Saint-Loup's 'libre et négligente élégance' 'plaisait tant à ma grand'mère' is a brief taste-attribution embedded within the already-captured collective admiration of Saint-Loup; it gives the grandmother no distinct local outcome of her own, so it was treated as part of the accepted movement rather than a separate event.
